trust_decision.summary: How deep the untrusted Lottie JSON shape tree may nest before recursion stops. At the pinned commit, parseGroupObject recurses through parseObject for every nested 'gr'/'it' with no depth limit. The existing kMaxModelTreeDepth guard sits only in post-parse model visitors.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'serialized data with nested payloads'. The JSON parser is the obvious place to look, and parseGroupObject->parseObject is its only self-recursive pair. rapidjson itself runs in iterative mode (src/lottie/lottieparser.cpp:391,408).

fix_sites.entry_point: rlottie::Animation::loadFromData / loadFromFile (src/lottie/lottieanimation.cpp:272,292,311) -> model::parse -> parseComposition -> parseLayer -> parseShapesAttr -> parseObject -> parseGroupObject; also the C API lottie_animation_from_data/from_file (src/binding/c/lottieanimation_capi.cpp:74,85)
same as above (new mGroupDepth member of LottieParserImpl, fix.diff:39)
none; the constant moves out of this file (fix.diff:13)
none; the constant moves into this header (fix.diff:25-26)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix changes behaviour only at parseGroupObject. The lottiemodel.cpp/.h hunks only move kMaxModelTreeDepth into the header (fix.diff:13,25-26).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Repeater chains are built from a FLAT 'it' array: no JSON nesting is present, the parser's group-depth cap is satisfied, and the repeater code already has copy and budget limits. A solver can argue that 'nested payload' recursion does not cover it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate files with shallow group nesting and several repeaters in one group must still parse and render; the fix.diff:56-58 behaviour skips only the too-deep 'it' subtree, which keeps the stream in sync for sibling keys/layers. An over-broad fix that rejects the whole composition, aborts parsing on depth, or caps or drops multi-repeater groups breaks real animations. The renderer also re-wraps repeater content and rounded-corner propagation walks nested groups.

O6_input_shapes: nested 'gr' shape groups via 'it' arrays inside layer 'shapes'
the same nesting inside precomp asset layers (assets[].layers[].shapes, src/lottie/lottieparser.cpp:993-1002)

O7_producer.where: src/lottie/lottiemodel.cpp:52-85 (LottieRepeaterProcesser::visitChildren turns a flat list containing N repeaters into an N-deep chain of repeater->content groups. The recursive call at line 79 bypasses the depth guard in visit() at line 92)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Repeater-chain nesting: a flat shape list with many 'rp' items is folded post-parse into a deep repeater->content tree. visitChildren recurses on it directly without the kMaxModelTreeDepth check, and the parser's group-depth counter never sees it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: No nested input exists, and the parser cap at the report's site is satisfied. The route looks like a repeater feature (already budget-limited), not 'nested payload' recursion.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file (lottiemodel.cpp vs lottieparser.cpp), runs after parse via model::parse at src/lottie/lottieparser.cpp:2583

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Renderer tree construction: createContentItem -> renderer::Group ctor -> addChildren -> createContentItem (and renderer::Repeater copies) recurses per model depth with no depth limit, bounded only by the 15000 content budget. The repeater chain above feeds it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The renderer already has budgets (kMaxShapeContentBudget, kMaxLayerDepth for precomp layers), and the parser cap bounds group depth to 32, so it looks already hardened.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file (lottieitem.cpp), runs at Animation construction (src/lottie/lottieitem.cpp:143-146)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second container shape type (e.g. a merge-path or text-group object carrying its own 'it' array) parsed via parseObject without touching mGroupDepth
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: parseObjectTypeAttr already dispatches 'mm' (merge path) as unsupported (line 1334-1336). A maintainer adding support would likely copy parseGroupObject's loop without the counter.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: updateRoundedCorner recursion over nested groups, if group nesting can arrive via a path other than parseGroupObject
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a recursive model walk inside the parser that never consults the depth constant.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: resolveKeyPath (public setValue keypath API) recursing over the renderer group tree with no depth guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A lower-level public API walking the same tree. The renderer's other walks (update/renderList/processPaintItems) are likewise unguarded.

O9_family: uncontrolled recursion (CWE-674) on nested shape-group tree from untrusted Lottie JSON

O10_build.toolchain: CMake or Meson; gtest for tests (test/testsuite.cpp)
O10_build.project_tests: test/test_lottieanimation.cpp and test/test_lottieanimation_capi.cpp load animations through the public API. The pinned tree has no depth or recursion tests. The fix diff adds no tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a depth counter to parseGroupObject only, considering the existing kMaxModelTreeDepth visitor guards sufficient for everything after parsing.

out_of_scope_notes: Layer parent-matrix recursion is already guarded at depth 64 (src/lottie/lottieitem.cpp:484-491); precomp cycles are handled in resolveLayerRefs (src/lottie/lottieparser.cpp:650-699).
Repeater copy explosion is resource exhaustion (budget at src/lottie/lottieitem.cpp:1591-1597), which is not pursued here.
